title: ZOE Plone end-to-end benchmark summary
description: The summary of one campaign of the Plone end-to-end benchmark (B5, ADR 0054): the runs of one fixture, at one commit, on one machine, with one set of settings, which `just bench plone report --json` writes. Results are numbers about a synthetic corpus, never data. It holds no host name, user name, path or password. A number that its counter does not give is null, never 0.

number.description: A number, or null when its counter does not give it.

switch.description: A switch of the merge policy, or null when the run did not write it.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema. A change that a reader of the previous version cannot read increments it.

machine.description: The machine that ran the campaign. It holds no host name, user name or path.

name.description: A stable name for the machine, used as a path segment in the results repository.

core_kinds.description: The physical cores of each kind of an Apple CPU, keyed by kind; null elsewhere.

cpu_pinning.description: How the processes are pinned to CPUs, such as taskset.

durability.description: How each server makes a commit durable, keyed by server.

store_disk.description: The disk that holds the stores of the runs.

python.description: The Python build of the Plone instances.

free_threaded.description: True for a build without the GIL, such as 3.14t.

gil_enabled.description: sys._is_gil_enabled() in an interpreter of the instances, or null when it is not known.

software.description: The version of each egg of the instances, of zoedb, of zoe serve and of Locust, keyed by name. A version that the runs did not record is absent.

started.description: When the first run of the campaign started, in UTC.

commit.description: The ZOE commit of the runs, or null when it is not known.

dirty.description: True when a run had a tree with changes that the commit does not hold; null when a run has no record of its tree; else false.

fixture.description: The synthetic site of every run of the campaign.

name.description: The name of the fixture, used as a path segment in the results repository.

preset.description: The preset whose SiteSpec equals the spec of the fixture, else custom.

objects.description: The content objects of the site, from the equivalence of its stores.

catalog_entries.description: The entries of the catalog, from the equivalence of its stores.

spec.description: The SiteSpec of the fixture: numbers and lists of numbers.

settings.description: The settings of every run of the campaign: the constants of the stacks without the ports and the switches, and the options of a run.

threads.description: The request threads of each instance.

zodb_cache_objects.description: The objects in the cache of each ZODB connection.

pool_size.description: The ZODB connections of each instance.

client_cache.description: The storage client cache of each instance.

server_cpus.description: The CPUs of the server, as a taskset list.

zope_cpus.description: The CPUs of each instance, as taskset lists.

locust_cpus.description: The CPUs of Locust, as a taskset list.

probe.description: True when the WSGI probe ran in the instances.

zeo_fsync.description: How the ZEO server syncs a commit on macOS.

zoe_cache_size.description: The --cache-size of zoe serve, or null for the default of the store.

zoe_compression.description: The --compression of zoe serve, or null for the default of the store.

trim_seconds.description: The seconds left out at the start of each step.

think.description: The min,max seconds between the operations of a user.

client_retries.description: The retries that Locust gives a failed write.

stacks.description: One entry per stack, in the order of the report.

server.description: The server: zeo (runzeo with a FileStorage) or zoe (zoe serve).

native.description: The key native of <zoeclient>, or null when the section does not have it.

backends.description: The backends of zoe.plone that the instances install.

member_properties.description: True when the properties of the members and groups are records of zoe.plone (ADR 0046).

merge_policy.description: The merge policy that the runs of the stack recorded, or null.

background.description: The background roles, one user each.

steps.description: One entry per scenario, stack and step: the numbers that the report prints, over the repetitions of the step.

step.description: The index of the step in the run.

seconds.description: The measured seconds of one repetition of the step, after the trim.

ok_per_second.description: The successful operations per second: the median, the lowest and the highest of the repetitions.

p50_seconds.description: The latency of a successful operation, pooled over the repetitions.

p99_reliable.description: True when the p99 comes from 200 operations or more.

first_attempt_share.description: The operations that succeeded at their first attempt, as a share of all.

conflicts_per_1000_ops.description: The ConflictErrors that the probe counts, per 1,000 operations.

exhausted.description: The requests whose retries of the publisher ran out.

zope_cpu_ms_per_op.description: The CPU of the instances per successful operation, in milliseconds.

server_cpu_ms_per_op.description: The CPU of the server per successful operation, in milliseconds.

store_write_kb_per_op.description: The KB that the server gives to the write calls of its store, per successful operation, or null when its counters do not give it. On zoe serve it is the growth of wchar minus the growth of the bytes of its TCP sockets and of its other files. The sampler reads the write counter and the socket counter one after the other, so on a step that writes almost nothing the value can fall a little below 0.

objects_loaded_per_second.description: The loadBefore calls that the probe counts for the operations of the step, over its seconds: the median of the repetitions.

objects_stored_per_second.description: The store calls that the probe counts for the operations of the step, over its seconds: the median of the repetitions.

runs.description: One entry per run, in the order of their start. A run without the numbers of its steps, such as a run that failed, has no entry in steps.

id.description: The run id: its start, its scenario, its stack and its repetition.

verification.description: The verdict of the verification of the run, or not run.

violations.description: The violations that the verification found, or null when it did not run.
